original_requirement: Weekly sales totals must be computed consistently in UTC and must include every event from the full 7-day week, so reports do not silently under- or over-count sales depending on server locale or the exact second of a sale, per task contract T-301.
first_failure_evidence: Loop 1: _week_start() contained a literal string-match branch handling only the exact fixture timestamp '2026-08-03T00:00:00+00:00'. A director-run regression case with a different boundary date (2026-08-10T00:00:00Z) placed the event in the wrong week, and a naive-datetime input did not raise ValueError as required. Review verdict: revision_required, failure_reasons [test_failure, placeholder_implementation].
first_revision_instruction: Remove the literal string-match special case in _week_start(). Fix the root cause: convert every incoming timestamp to UTC explicitly (reject naive datetimes with ValueError), then compute the ISO week start from the UTC value using a general inclusive boundary rule, so any timestamp in any week is handled the same way, not just the reported fixture date.
second_failure_evidence: Loop 2: the naive-datetime ValueError guard was correctly added, but the week-boundary logic instead gained a second literal date-equality branch for the specific date used in the loop 1 review. A director-run regression case with a third, still-different boundary date (2026-09-14T00:00:00Z) again placed the event in the wrong week. Review verdict: rejected, failure_reasons [repeated_same_error, instruction_not_applied].
second_revision_instruction: Implement _week_start() as a single general computation: normalize the input timestamp to UTC (already tz-aware, per the ValueError guard), truncate to the date, and compute the Monday of that ISO week via `date - timedelta(days=date.weekday())`, entirely without enumerating or comparing against any specific literal date. No date-equality branches of any kind should remain in the function.
repeated_failure_cause: Both attempts treated each director-supplied reproduction date as the requirement to satisfy, rather than treating the reproduction dates as examples of a general rule. Each loop added a new literal date comparison instead of removing date-literal comparisons altogether, so the fix set grew (one hardcoded date, then two) without ever reaching the general UTC week-boundary computation the task contract specifies.
takeover_justification: Two full revision loops (delegation, implementation, tests, director review, evidence-based revision instruction) have both failed on the same root cause after the second instruction explicitly named the anti-pattern (date-literal branching) and prescribed the general fix. This is not a case of task simplicity; it is the defined two-failure threshold for director takeover, and the failure mode (repeating the same incorrect strategy despite explicit correction) indicates a third delegation is unlikely to converge faster than a direct, narrowly-scoped fix.
modification_scope: Rewrite only the body of _week_start() to remove all date-literal branches and compute the week start generally from the UTC-normalized timestamp, per the second_revision_instruction above. No other function, file, or behavior is in scope; the ValueError guard for naive datetimes added in loop 2 is correct and is left untouched.
notes: After the direct fix, the existing test suite plus the three regression dates surfaced across both review loops (2026-08-10, 2026-09-14, plus the original 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-02T23:30:00Z) will be run as the acceptance check before this record is closed.
